summary: Maps HDR image values down to an SDR display range using selectable artistic tone-mapping curves.

key_params.name: type
key_params.note: Tone-mapping curve such as ACES, Lottes, Filmic, Hable Filmic, Reinhard, or Extended Reinhard

key_params.name: midinputnits
key_params.note: Estimated input mid brightness in nits

key_params.name: peakinputnits
key_params.note: Estimated input peak brightness in nits

key_params.name: exposurebias
key_params.note: Artistic exposure bias for Hable Filmic

common_gotchas: Do not use Tone Map TOP when outputting to an HDR display with HDR mode enabled.
There is no universally correct tone-map type; choose by content and visual preference.
Peak Input Nits can be estimated or measured with Analyze TOP for better control.
Mid Input Nits measured through Analyze or Monochrome TOP must account for Reference White scaling.
Tone mapping preserves visible differences for SDR output but does not preserve true physical brightness.
key_concepts: Tone Map TOP maps HDR values above 1.0 into an SDR 0-1 range.
The Type menu chooses an artistic tone-mapping curve rather than a single physically correct conversion.
Mid and peak nit parameters describe the input and output brightness assumptions used by the selected curve.
The official docs warn that Tone Map TOP is not intended for HDR display output when HDR output mode is active.
